description: PIA is the Eclipse Foundation's OIDC authentication broker for SBOM uploads to DependencyTrack. A CI job (GitHub Actions, Eclipse GitLab CI, or a registered Jenkins pipeline) posts an SBOM with a short-lived OIDC token; PIA verifies the token against the allowlisted issuer's JWKS, maps the verified identity to a registered Eclipse Foundation project, and relays the SBOM to that project's DependencyTrack target with PIA's own API key. It runs as one uvicorn worker per pod behind a TLS-terminating, rate-limiting reverse proxy; operators manage registrations with the `pia sync` CLI from a curated YAML file.

properties_provided.conditions: RS256 only; key fetched per request from the allowlisted issuer's JWKS, kid match, use sig or absent; aud equals PIA_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE; exp unexpired; iat present
iss equals the GitHub issuer, the Eclipse GitLab issuer, or a registered Jenkins issuer; jwks_uri under {iss}/ with unreserved characters and no dot segments; no redirects; HTTP 200 only
each discovery and JWKS response: 10 s per read, 1 MiB decoded cap, 10 s deadline checked between reads; total wall time is not bounded (D-SLOW-RETRIEVAL)

verified claims match exactly one registered workload; GitHub event_name a string in {push, workflow_dispatch, release, schedule}; GitLab matched on project_path and project_id (never job_project_*), so fork MR pipelines never match and a project re-created at a registered path is rejected until re-synced, against insiders too (maintainer 2026-11); GitLab pipeline_source a string in {push, web, schedule, api}; product_name resolved only within the workload's ef_project_id; registrations are operator input

known_misuse.pattern: a workflow_dispatch or push workflow checks out and runs pull-request code, giving it a token PIA accepts
known_misuse.why_unsafe: PIA sees a maintainer event and stops there; the token is minted for whatever code the workflow runs
known_misuse.instead: keep publishing workflows free of untrusted inputs

known_misuse.pattern: a deleted or renamed repository's name is re-created under the same owner and inherits the registration
known_misuse.why_unsafe: GitHub workloads are matched on owner id plus names, not repository_id, so a re-created repo silently becomes the publisher (GitLab workloads are pinned by project_id)
known_misuse.instead: treat repo deletion or rename as a pia sync event; repository_id matching is planned as hardening

known_misuse.pattern: two spellings of one repository registered under two EF projects
known_misuse.why_unsafe: GitHub names are case-insensitive, so only one row ever matches and the policy no longer says what it means; GitLab paths are checked for canonical spelling at sync

known_misuse.pattern: exposing port 8000 directly: plain HTTP, no rate limit, no body cap
known_misuse.why_unsafe: PIA provides no TLS, rate limiting or body cap of its own
known_misuse.instead: deploy behind the reverse proxy per §1.13

known_misuse.pattern: treating the DependencyTrack API key as per-project; a portfolio-management key in the app pod
known_misuse.why_unsafe: DependencyTrack trusts PIA wholesale, so a wide key widens the blast radius of any PIA bug

known_misuse.pattern: retrying an upload after a 500 when the SBOM may already be stored
known_misuse.why_unsafe: a 500 after a 2xx from DependencyTrack means the SBOM was likely stored; a retry duplicates it
known_misuse.instead: poll DependencyTrack for the version before re-sending

known_misuse.pattern: running uvicorn with --workers so metrics become per-worker and wrong
known_misuse.why_unsafe: each worker keeps its own Prometheus registry, so /metrics reports one worker's view

known_non_findings.reported_as: JWT decoded with verify_signature=False in pia/main.py authenticate
known_non_findings.why_safe: Against auth, the integrity-bypass symptom is discharged by the claimed property P-SIG: the unverified claims are used only to select the issuer allowlist row; every authorization decision uses the claims returned by the verifying decode.
known_non_findings.suppression: the unverified claims are used only to select the issuer allowlist row; every authorization decision uses the claims returned by the verifying decode

known_non_findings.reported_as: no rate limiting on /v1/upload/sbom; each request triggers outbound fetches
known_non_findings.why_safe: Against auth, upload-relay, ops-endpoints, the x-volumetric-dos symptom is discharged by the disclaimed property D-RATE-LIMIT: the report shows only request volume, not a per-request bound being exceeded.
known_non_findings.suppression: the report shows only request volume, not a per-request bound being exceeded

known_non_findings.reported_as: slow or trickling issuer holds a worker beyond 10 s
known_non_findings.why_safe: Against auth, the x-worker-exhaustion symptom is discharged by the disclaimed property D-SLOW-RETRIEVAL: the slow party is a registered issuer, and the event loop and /livez keep serving.
known_non_findings.suppression: the slow party is a registered issuer, and the event loop and /livez keep serving

known_non_findings.reported_as: request method or path used as a Prometheus label
known_non_findings.why_safe: Against ops-endpoints, the unbounded-allocation symptom is discharged by the claimed property P-METRIC-CARD: the value passes through method_label, the route template, a Literal, or a database row before labeling.
known_non_findings.suppression: the value passes through method_label, the route template, a Literal, or a database row before labeling

known_non_findings.reported_as: a valid token can be reused within its lifetime
known_non_findings.why_safe: Against auth, the x-token-replay symptom is discharged by the disclaimed property D-REPLAY: the replayed token is unexpired and the report shows no acceptance past exp.
known_non_findings.suppression: the replayed token is unexpired and the report shows no acceptance past exp
